name: Blackberry Galette
why: Blackberries are at peak season right now, and a galette is the laziest, most forgiving way to show them off - no pastry cases, no rolling rings, just free-form folding. Golden flaky crust around bubbling fruit, served with vanilla ice cream: classic late-summer dessert done right.
author: Henry
ingredients: 115g cold butter, frozen and finely shredded
150g plain flour (plus a little to dust)
150g caster sugar (plus a little extra for sprinkling)
vanilla bean ice cream, to serve

steps: Stir the flour and salt together in a large bowl or food processor.
Add the cold, shredded butter (freezing it first keeps the pieces sharp) and pulse until the mixture resembles coarse meal with small pea-sized butter bits.
Drizzle in the ice-cold water 1-2 tablespoons at a time, adding the vinegar, and pulse until the dough just starts to come together - do not overwork it.
Press the dough into a ball, pat into a disk, wrap tightly in cling film and chill for at least 30 minutes (2 hours preferred).
Toss the blackberries with the 30g flour and 150g sugar, and the lemon juice. Set aside.
Roll the dough on a lightly floured surface to about 35cm across and 3mm thick - do not overwork it. Transfer to a lightly greased baking sheet.
Mound the berries in the centre, leaving a 4cm border of dough.
Fold the edges up and around the fruit, pinching together to make deep pleats around the edge.
Brush the pleats with beaten egg and sprinkle over a little extra sugar.
Bake in a preheated 190C fan oven (375F) for 40-44 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the fruit is bubbling.
Check often from the 30-minute mark and lift the galette with a spatula to check the underside is cooking evenly.
Rest for 15 minutes, then slice into 12 and serve with vanilla bean ice cream.

pro_tips: Keep the butter frozen until you cut it in - sharp cold shards are what make the pastry shatter, and a warm kitchen is the enemy of flakiness.
The 30g of flour in the filling is not a mistake: it thickens the juice the berries release in the oven so the centre sets instead of running. Don't skip it.
